newsitem.title: USA: Legislation would cut Florida Turnpike revenues.
newsitem.headline: Legislation would cut Florida Turnpike revenues.

text.p: A Florida lawmaker has introduced a bill that would speed repayment of $1.317 billion of state turnpike revenue bonds, and then limit toll collections to the amount needed for turnpike maintenance.
The bill (SB1260) by Sen. Mario Diaz-Balart, R-Miami, is pending before the Senate Transportation and Ways and Means committees.
Its aim is to stop the use of the turnpike as a revenue generator for road projects unrelated to the turnpike system, an aide to Diaz-Balart said Wednesday.
The 345-mile turnpike, which opened in 1957, runs from just north of the Florida Keys on the southeast coast to Wildwood in north central Florida.
The construction bonds were paid off long ago but tolls are still collected and much of the money is leveraved via revenue bonds to finance unrelated transportation projects.
"Some of these projects are in Jacksonville, Tampa. It's going to fund roads that don't even attach to the turnpike," the aide said.

Gross turnpike revenues for fiscal 1996 were $231.8 million. Of that, $68.9 million went toward turnpike operations, $78.1 million was used for debt service and the remaining $84.8 million was earmarked other transportation projects.

Diaz-Balart's bill would require that all toll revenues in excess of that needed for operations and maintenance, and not already pledged to debt service, be used to expedite repayment of the outstanding bonds.
Once all the bonds are retired, tolls would be eliminated, except for the amount needed for operations and maintenance.
Bonding capacity from turnpike revenues is capped at $1.5 billion. With $1.317 billion of turnpike revenue bond outstanding, the state still has unused capacity of $182 million.
State transportation officials were not immediately available for comment on the bill. Sen. Jim Horne, R-Orange Park, told the Jacksonville Times-Union that, "Economically, it would be devastating."
